about: History's aims for the great realms (your answers 'Each realm has history's aims, weighted by the history pull', 'A few aims per realm per era, sourced' and 'Great powers first'). An aim is land a realm wanted in those years, in the 38 ancient regions: while it holds less than half of the aim's provinces, it presses there in its wars, and, strong and at peace with no campaign due, it may make war for it. History's campaigns (history_goals.json) are the wars that happened; aims are the wants behind them, and they keep pulling when history goes another way. An aim dies with its realm. Sources are the ancient authors (book.chapter), with a modern reference where the ancient text is thin.

aims.aim: All Italy south of the Po
aims.why: After the Latin and Samnite wars Rome meant to lead every people of the peninsula, by treaty or by conquest.
The island between Italy and Africa: whoever held Messana held the strait.
Carthage's silver mines and soldiers, then the long wars against the Celtiberians and Lusitanians.
Illyrian piracy, then fear of Philip V and the kings of Macedon across the narrow sea.
'Carthage must be destroyed': Cato's demand, carried out in the Third Punic War.
aims.source: Plutarch, Cato the Elder 27; Appian, Punica 69-135

aims.why: Left to Rome by Attalus III of Pergamon, and defended against Mithridates.
First the road to Spain along the coast, then all Gaul under Caesar.
Pompey's settlement of the East: the last Seleucid lands as a Roman province.
The grain of the Nile, taken by Octavian after Actium.
Carthage's trading cities on the island, held against the Greeks for two centuries.

aims.aim: Mastery of the Libyan and Numidian lands
aims.why: The farms of the hinterland fed the city; the Numidian horse fought for it.
After losing Sicily, Hamilcar Barca built a new realm in Spain to pay the indemnity and raise armies.
Promised to Seleucus after Ipsus but seized by Ptolemy: the cause of six Syrian Wars.
Won from Lysimachus at Corupedium, lost to Rome at Magnesia.
The heart of the kingdom: Babylon, Seleucia on the Tigris and the roads east, held until the Parthians took them.
Antiochus III crossed to Europe claiming Lysimachus' old kingdom, which brought him to war with Rome.
Held since Ipsus as a shield for the Nile and for its timber and trade.
The Greek cities west of the Delta, ruled by Ptolemy's stepson Magas and won back by marriage.
Ports won in the Third Syrian War to guard the sea routes.
Kassander's house held Macedon and garrisoned the Greek cities.
Demetrius and his heirs wanted back the kingdom of Philip and Alexander, and the Greek cities with it.
His share after Ipsus, held from Lysimacheia on the Hellespont.
Shared with Pyrrhus after Demetrius fell, then taken whole.
Pyrrhus twice won and lost the Macedonian throne.
Called in by Tarentum, Pyrrhus dreamed of Italy, then Sicily, then Africa: so Cineas reports him.
From Agathocles to Hieron, Syracuse's kings meant to rule the island and drive out Carthage.
